sections.crash_profile: During {{window_start}} to {{window_end}}, {{ka_3y}} fatal or serious injury crashes and {{kabc_3y}} KABCO injury crashes occurred at this signalized four-leg intersection. The most frequent crash types were left-turn opposing, rear-end, and run-off-road. Night and wet conditions were noted in several crashes. Pedestrian and bicycle counts are not available.
sections.why_flagged: Flagged due to a model-estimated fatal or serious injury crash rate of {{fsi_rate}} per mile and {{annual_fsi}} per year. High traffic exposure ({{aadt}} vehicles/day), multiple marked crossings, four-leg geometry, and a concentration of crashes within {{length_mi}} miles also contributed. The site ranks {{rank_city_actionable}} among actionable city intersections and is included in the high-injury network.

countermeasures.rationale: Providing a left-turn lane on one major-road approach is supported by broader evidence for all severities at four-leg urban signalized intersections. The cited CMF {{cmf:267}} is an aggregate match for all crash types, but does not directly establish a reduction for fatal or serious injury crashes and requires engineering review.

Adding 3-inch yellow retroreflective sheeting to signal backplates is supported by broader evidence for all severities at urban signalized intersections. The cited CMF {{cmf:1410}} is an aggregate match for all crash types, but does not directly establish a reduction for fatal or serious injury crashes and requires engineering review.

sections.benefit_cost: A benefit could not be computed for any countermeasure. The library lacks audit-approved CMFs for fatal or serious injury crashes, planning-level unit costs, and service life values for these treatments.
sections.next_steps: Review site geometry, traffic volumes, and existing equipment to confirm eligibility for the proposed countermeasures. Conduct engineering review to assess feasibility and applicability, especially for left-turn lane provision and signal backplate enhancements. Confirm prerequisites and coordinate with TxDOT as needed.
